"The market research team has reached out to you and the team behind data analysis. They are hoping to do some research on the current game instudry to find out what Category/ Style of game should be made and what the price and the best release date the game should have for the best result in sales post game launch. "¶

About the data¶

The data has been harvested by the Github user 'NewbieIndieGameDev/steam-insights' In the description of the video it lists places to get steam store data through API's an example of the API's used by NewbieIndieGameDev is the 'SteamSPY' API. These numbers can be found in the reviews dataset below.

I will not be using any API's or the api sections of the data on the github for this Analysis and will only be using the data thats already been scraped by NewbieIndieGameDev Future development could include API's live data in the future

Project Objectives and business questions¶

  • What are some trends that occur based on game price and game category
  • Do games in certain categories sell better than others or are there too many external factors to determine this
  • Based on the Analysis are there any gaps in the market that could be harnessed
  • Does release date have an effect on post launch sales

  • Does release date have any impact on long term sales

General information¶

This is an analysis of the steam store. This is a passion project and has been done due to my own interest in games. The data was found from a video online and a github provided in the description. All the data was harnessed by the channel "Newbie Indie Game Dev" and the data can be found on my Github or his

# Comprehensive Steam Games Data Cleaning
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import re

# Load the CSV file
df = pd.read_csv('games.csv', encoding='utf-8')

# Function to extract price and currency information
def combine_price_info(row):
    price_info = {}
    
    # Extract initial price from Initial_price column
    if pd.notna(row['Initial_price']):
        # Try different regex patterns to match the price format
        price_match = re.search(r'"initial":\s*(\d+)', str(row['Initial_price']))
        if not price_match:
            price_match = re.search(r'initial\\?":\s*(\d+)', str(row['Initial_price']))
        if price_match:
            price_info['initial'] = int(price_match.group(1))
    
    # Extract currency from currency column
    if pd.notna(row['currency']):
        # Try different regex patterns to match currency format
        currency_match = re.search(r'"currency":\s*"([^"]+)"', str(row['currency']))
        if not currency_match:
            currency_match = re.search(r'currency\\?":\s*\\?"([^\\",]+)\\?"', str(row['currency']))
        if currency_match:
            price_info['currency'] = currency_match.group(1)
    
    return price_info  # This was missing in your original code!

# Apply the function to create a new column with the combined price information
df['price_info'] = df.apply(combine_price_info, axis=1)

# Extract individual price components
df['price'] = df['price_info'].apply(lambda x: x.get('initial') if isinstance(x, dict) else np.nan)
df['currency_clean'] = df['price_info'].apply(lambda x: x.get('currency') if isinstance(x, dict) else np.nan)

# Convert release_date to datetime
df['release_date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['release_date'], errors='coerce', dayfirst=True)

# Convert is_free to boolean (handle string 'True'/'False' values)
df['is_free'] = df['is_free'].astype(str).str.lower().map({'true': True, 'false': False, '1': True, '0': False})

# Create a clean dataframe with only the columns we need
clean_columns = ['app_id', 'name', 'release_date', 'is_free', 'price', 'currency_clean', 'type']

# Only include columns that actually exist in the dataframe
existing_columns = [col for col in clean_columns if col in df.columns]
df_games_clean = df[existing_columns].copy()

# Rename columns for clarity
df_games_clean.rename(columns={'currency_clean': 'currency'}, inplace=True)

# Convert price to appropriate numeric format (assuming prices are in cents)
# You might want to divide by 100 to get the actual price in major currency units
df_games_clean['price'] = df_games_clean['price'] / 100

# Remove rows where price extraction failed for paid games
# Keep free games even if price extraction failed
df_games_clean = df_games_clean[
    (df_games_clean['is_free'] == True) | 
    (df_games_clean['price'].notna())
]

# Save the cleaned data to a new CSV file
df_games_clean.to_csv('games_cleaned.csv', index=False)

print("Data cleaning completed and saved to 'games_cleaned.csv'")
print(f"Original shape: {df.shape}, Cleaned shape: {df_games_clean.shape}")
print("\nMissing values in cleaned data:")
print(df_games_clean.isnull().sum())
print("\nSample of cleaned data:")
print(df_games_clean.head())
print("\nPrice statistics:")
print(df_games_clean['price'].describe())
print(f"\nUnique currencies: {df_games_clean['currency'].unique()}")

def is_non_numeric(value):
    if pd.isna(value) or isinstance(value, (int, float)):  # Allow NaN and numeric types
        return False
    return not str(value).replace('.', '', 1).isdigit()  # Check if non-numeric

# Apply function and sum occurrences

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Create the plot using your actual dataframe
plt.figure(figsize=(16, 10))

# Get value counts from your dataframe
review_counts = df_reviews_cleaned['review_score_description'].value_counts()

# Create bar plot
bars = plt.bar(range(len(review_counts)), review_counts.values, color='steelblue', alpha=0.7)

# Customize the plot
plt.title('Steam Game Review Score Distribution - Raw Data\n(Shows Why Data Cleaning is Needed!)', 
          fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Review Score Description', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
plt.ylabel('Number of Games', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Set x-axis labels with rotation for readability
plt.xticks(range(len(review_counts)), review_counts.index, rotation=45, ha='right')

# Add value labels on top of bars
for i, bar in enumerate(bars):
    height = bar.get_height()
    plt.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height + max(review_counts.values) * 0.01,
             f'{int(height):,}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=9)

# Add grid for better readability
plt.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')

# Color code different types of entries to highlight the problems
categories = review_counts.index.tolist()
for i, category in enumerate(categories):
    if 'user reviews' in category or category in ['No user reviews', '\\N']:
        bars[i].set_color('red')
        bars[i].set_alpha(0.8)
    elif category in ['Overwhelmingly Positive', 'Very Positive', 'Mostly Positive', 'Positive']:
        bars[i].set_color('green')
        bars[i].set_alpha(0.7)
    elif category in ['Mixed']:
        bars[i].set_color('orange')
        bars[i].set_alpha(0.7)
    elif category in ['Mostly Negative', 'Negative', 'Very Negative', 'Overwhelmingly Negative']:
        bars[i].set_color('darkred')
        bars[i].set_alpha(0.7)

# Add legend to explain the color coding

def clean_review_data(df, review_col='review_score_description'):
    
    print("BEFORE CLEANING:")
    print("=" * 40)
    print(f"Total games: {len(df):,}")
    print(f"Unique review categories: {df[review_col].nunique()}")
    print("\nOriginal distribution:")
    original_counts = df[review_col].value_counts()
    print(original_counts)
    
    # Create a copy to work with
    df_clean = df.copy()
    
    # Step 1: Drop games with '\N' review descriptions
    print(f"\nStep 1: Dropping games with '\\N' review descriptions...")
    null_games = len(df_clean[df_clean[review_col] == '\\N'])
    print(f"Games to drop: {null_games:,}")
    
    df_clean = df_clean[df_clean[review_col] != '\\N'].copy()
    
    # Step 2: Group 1-9 user reviews into 'Few Reviews (1-9)'
    print(f"\nStep 2: Grouping 1-9 user review categories...")
    
    # Create mapping for review descriptions
    def standardize_review_description(description):
        if pd.isna(description):
            return description
        
        desc_str = str(description).strip()
        
        # Group all variations of 1-9 user reviews
        if 'user reviews' in desc_str and any(str(i) in desc_str for i in range(1, 10)):
            return 'Few Reviews (1-9)'
        
        # Standardize 'No user reviews' to 'No Reviews'
        elif desc_str == 'No user reviews':
            return 'No Reviews'
        
        # Keep other categories as-is (they should already be standard)
        else:
            return desc_str
    
    # Apply the standardization
    df_clean[review_col] = df_clean[review_col].apply(standardize_review_description)
    
    # Step 3: Show what categories we grouped
    few_review_categories = original_counts[original_counts.index.str.contains('user reviews', na=False)]
    few_review_categories = few_review_categories[~few_review_categories.index.str.contains('No user reviews', na=False)]
    
    if len(few_review_categories) > 0:
        print("Categories grouped into 'Few Reviews (1-9)':")
        total_few_reviews = 0
        for category, count in few_review_categories.items():
            print(f"  → {category}: {count:,} games")
            total_few_reviews += count
        print(f"Total games in 'Few Reviews (1-9)': {total_few_reviews:,}")
    
    print("\nAFTER CLEANING:")
    print("=" * 40)
    print(f"Total games: {len(df_clean):,}")
    print(f"Games dropped: {len(df) - len(df_clean):,}")
    print(f"Unique review categories: {df_clean[review_col].nunique()}")
    
    print("\nFinal distribution:")
    final_counts = df_clean[review_col].value_counts()
    print(final_counts)
    
    return df_clean

# Apply the cleaning to your dataframe
print("Cleaning your Steam review data...")
df_reviews_final = clean_review_data(df_reviews_cleaned, 'review_score_description')

# Create bar plot
bars = plt.bar(range(len(review_counts)), review_counts.values, alpha=0.8)

# Customize the plot
plt.title('Steam Game Review Score Distribution - After Cleaning\n(Grouped Few Reviews, Dropped \\N Games)', 
          fontsize=16, fontweight='bold', pad=20)
plt.xlabel('Review Score Description', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
plt.ylabel('Number of Games', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')

# Set x-axis labels with rotation for readability
plt.xticks(range(len(review_counts)), review_counts.index, rotation=45, ha='right')

# Add value labels on top of bars
for i, bar in enumerate(bars):
    height = bar.get_height()
    plt.text(bar.get_x() + bar.get_width()/2., height + max(review_counts.values) * 0.01,
             f'{int(height):,}', ha='center', va='bottom', fontsize=10, fontweight='bold')

# Add grid for better readability
plt.grid(axis='y', alpha=0.3, linestyle='--')

# Color code the bars based on review sentiment
categories = review_counts.index.tolist()
colors = []
for i, category in enumerate(categories):
    if category in ['Few Reviews (1-9)', 'No Reviews']:
        bars[i].set_color('gray')
        bars[i].set_alpha(0.6)
    elif category in ['Overwhelmingly Positive', 'Very Positive', 'Mostly Positive', 'Positive']:
        bars[i].set_color('green')
        bars[i].set_alpha(0.8)
    elif category in ['Mixed']:
        bars[i].set_color('orange')
        bars[i].set_alpha(0.8)
    elif category in ['Mostly Negative', 'Negative', 'Very Negative', 'Overwhelmingly Negative']:
        bars[i].set_color('darkred')
        bars[i].set_alpha(0.8)

# Add legend

]

def clean_multilingual_categories(df, category_column='categories'):
   """
   Clean multilingual Steam categories by:
   1. Translating non-English terms to English
   2. Standardizing format
   3. Removing duplicates
   """
   df_clean = df.copy()
   
   def translate_categories(category_string):
       if pd.isna(category_string):
           return np.nan
       
       if isinstance(category_string, str):
           categories = [cat.strip() for cat in category_string.split(',')]
       else:
           categories = [str(category_string)]
       
       translated_categories = []
       for cat in categories:
           cat_clean = cat.strip().replace('\xa0', ' ')
           
           if cat_clean in category_translation_map:
               translated_categories.append(category_translation_map[cat_clean])
           else:
               translated_categories.append(cat_clean)
       
       unique_categories = list(dict.fromkeys(translated_categories))
       return ', '.join(unique_categories)
   
   df_clean[f'{category_column}_english'] = df_clean[category_column].apply(translate_categories)
   
   return df_clean

# Apply the cleaning function
df_cat_cleaned = clean_multilingual_categories(df_cat, 'category')

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import numpy as np
from datetime import datetime

# Set up plotting style
plt.style.use('default')
sns.set_palette("husl")

# ============================================================================
# 1. PRICE AND CATEGORY TRENDS
# ============================================================================

def analyze_price_category_trends():
    """
    Analyze trends between game price and categories
    """
    print("=== 1. PRICE AND CATEGORY TRENDS ===")
    
    # Merge games with categories and reviews
    price_category_data = df_games_clean.merge(df_cat_cleaned, on='app_id', how='left')\
                                       .merge(df_reviews_final, on='app_id', how='left')
    
    # Price distribution by category (top categories only)
    top_categories = price_category_data['category_english'].value_counts().head(10).index
    filtered_data = price_category_data[price_category_data['category_english'].isin(top_categories)]
    
    # Remove outliers for better visualization (games over $100)
    filtered_data = filtered_data[filtered_data['price'] <= 100]
    
    print(f"Average price by category (top 10 categories):")
    avg_price_by_category = filtered_data.groupby('category_english')['price'].agg(['mean', 'median', 'count']).round(2)
    print(avg_price_by_category.sort_values('mean', ascending=False))
    
    # Price vs Review Score correlation by category
    print(f"\nPrice vs Review Score correlation by category:")
    price_review_corr = filtered_data.groupby('category_english').apply(
        lambda x: x['price'].corr(x['review_score'])
    ).round(3)
    print(price_review_corr.sort_values(ascending=False))
    
    return filtered_data

# ============================================================================
# 2. CATEGORY PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

def analyze_category_performance():
    """
    Determine which categories perform better and identify external factors
    """
    print("\n=== 2. CATEGORY PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS ===")
    
    # Merge all relevant data
    performance_data = df_games_clean.merge(df_cat_cleaned, on='app_id', how='left')\
                                    .merge(df_reviews_final, on='app_id', how='left')\
                                    .merge(df_genres, on='app_id', how='left')
    
    # Performance metrics by category
    category_performance = performance_data.groupby('category_english').agg({
        'review_score': ['mean', 'count'],
        'total': 'mean',  # Average total reviews (proxy for sales)
        'positive': 'mean',
        'price': 'mean'
    }).round(2)
    
    category_performance.columns = ['avg_review_score', 'game_count', 'avg_total_reviews', 
                                   'avg_positive_reviews', 'avg_price']
    
    # Filter categories with at least 10 games for reliability
    category_performance = category_performance[category_performance['game_count'] >= 10]
    category_performance = category_performance.sort_values('avg_total_reviews', ascending=False)
    
    print("Category Performance (sorted by average total reviews):")
    print(category_performance.head(15))
    
    # Success rate (games with >8.0 review score) by category
    print(f"\nSuccess Rate by Category (% with review_score > 8.0):")
    success_rate = performance_data.groupby('category_english').apply(
        lambda x: (x['review_score'] > 8.0).mean() * 100
    ).round(1).sort_values(ascending=False)
    print(success_rate.head(10))
    
    return performance_data, category_performance

# ============================================================================
# 3. MARKET GAP ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

def identify_market_gaps():
    """
    Identify potential market gaps based on category/genre combinations
    """
    print("\n=== 3. MARKET GAP ANALYSIS ===")
    
    # Create genre-category combinations
    gap_data = df_games_clean.merge(df_cat_cleaned, on='app_id', how='left')\
                            .merge(df_genres, on='app_id', how='left')\
                            .merge(df_reviews_final, on='app_id', how='left')
    
    # Analyze genre-category combinations
    genre_category_combo = gap_data.groupby(['genre', 'category_english']).agg({
        'app_id': 'count',
        'review_score': 'mean',
        'total': 'mean',
        'price': 'mean'
    }).round(2)
    
    genre_category_combo.columns = ['game_count', 'avg_review_score', 'avg_total_reviews', 'avg_price']
    
    # Identify potential gaps: high-performing combinations with few games
    potential_gaps = genre_category_combo[
        (genre_category_combo['game_count'] < 20) & 
        (genre_category_combo['avg_review_score'] > 7.5) &
        (genre_category_combo['avg_total_reviews'] > 1000)
    ].sort_values('avg_review_score', ascending=False)
    
    print("Potential Market Gaps (High performance, low competition):")
    print(potential_gaps.head(10))
    
    # Oversaturated markets
    oversaturated = genre_category_combo[
        genre_category_combo['game_count'] > 100
    ].sort_values('game_count', ascending=False)
    
    print(f"\nOversaturated Markets (>100 games):")
    print(oversaturated.head(10))
    
    return gap_data, potential_gaps

# ============================================================================
# 4. RELEASE DATE IMPACT ON POST-LAUNCH PERFORMANCE
# ============================================================================

def analyze_release_date_impact():
    """
    Analyze how release date affects post-launch sales and performance
    """
    print("\n=== 4. RELEASE DATE IMPACT ANALYSIS ===")
    
    # Prepare data with release dates
    release_data = df_games_clean.merge(df_reviews_final, on='app_id', how='left')
    release_data['release_date'] = pd.to_datetime(release_data['release_date'])
    release_data['release_year'] = release_data['release_date'].dt.year
    release_data['release_month'] = release_data['release_date'].dt.month
    
    # Filter reasonable date range (Steam era)
    release_data = release_data[release_data['release_year'] >= 2004]
    release_data = release_data[release_data['release_year'] <= 2024]
    
    # Performance by release year
    yearly_performance = release_data.groupby('release_year').agg({
        'review_score': 'mean',
        'total': 'mean',
        'positive': 'mean',
        'price': 'mean',
        'app_id': 'count'
    }).round(2)
    
    yearly_performance.columns = ['avg_review_score', 'avg_total_reviews', 
                                 'avg_positive_reviews', 'avg_price', 'games_released']
    
    print("Performance by Release Year:")
    print(yearly_performance.tail(10))  # Last 10 years
    
    # Monthly seasonality
    monthly_performance = release_data.groupby('release_month').agg({
        'review_score': 'mean',
        'total': 'mean',
        'app_id': 'count'
    }).round(2)
    
    print(f"\nMonthly Release Patterns:")
    month_names = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun',
                   'Jul', 'Aug', 'Sep', 'Oct', 'Nov', 'Dec']
    monthly_performance.index = month_names
    print(monthly_performance)
    
    return release_data, yearly_performance

# ============================================================================
# 5. LONG-TERM SALES ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

def analyze_long_term_trends():
    """
    Analyze long-term sales trends and sustainability
    """
    print("\n=== 5. LONG-TERM SALES TRENDS ===")
    
    # Create age categories for games
    current_year = 2024
    long_term_data = df_games_clean.merge(df_reviews_final, on='app_id', how='left')
    long_term_data['release_date'] = pd.to_datetime(long_term_data['release_date'])
    long_term_data['game_age'] = current_year - long_term_data['release_date'].dt.year
    
    # Filter reasonable ranges
    long_term_data = long_term_data[
        (long_term_data['game_age'] >= 0) & 
        (long_term_data['game_age'] <= 20)
    ]
    
    # Age categories
    def age_category(age):
        if age <= 1:
            return 'New (0-1 years)'
        elif age <= 3:
            return 'Recent (1-3 years)'
        elif age <= 7:
            return 'Established (3-7 years)'
        else:
            return 'Legacy (7+ years)'
    
    long_term_data['age_category'] = long_term_data['game_age'].apply(age_category)
    
    # Performance by age category
    age_performance = long_term_data.groupby('age_category').agg({
        'review_score': 'mean',
        'total': 'mean',
        'positive': 'mean',
        'price': 'mean',
        'app_id': 'count'
    }).round(2)
    
    print("Performance by Game Age:")
    print(age_performance)
    
    # Long-term sustainability analysis
    print(f"\nLong-term Sustainability Indicators:")
    sustainability = long_term_data[long_term_data['game_age'] >= 5].groupby('age_category').agg({
        'total': 'mean',
        'review_score': 'mean'
    }).round(2)
    
    print(sustainability)
    
    return long_term_data

# ============================================================================
# EXECUTE ALL ANALYSES
# ============================================================================

def run_complete_analysis():
    """
    Run all business analyses
    """
    print("STEAM GAMES MARKET ANALYSIS")
    print("=" * 50)
    
    # Run all analyses
    price_data = analyze_price_category_trends()
    perf_data, cat_perf = analyze_category_performance()
    gap_data, gaps = identify_market_gaps()
    release_data, yearly_perf = analyze_release_date_impact()
    long_term_data = analyze_long_term_trends()
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 50)
    print("BUSINESS RECOMMENDATIONS:")
    print("=" * 50)
    
    print("1. PRICING STRATEGY:")
    print("   - Monitor high-performing categories for optimal pricing")
    print("   - Consider premium pricing for specialized categories")
    
    print("2. MARKET OPPORTUNITIES:")
    print("   - Focus on identified gap areas with high performance/low competition")
    print("   - Avoid oversaturated markets unless you have unique differentiators")
    
    print("3. RELEASE TIMING:")
    print("   - Consider seasonal patterns for optimal launch timing")
    print("   - Account for market saturation in recent years")
    
    print("4. LONG-TERM STRATEGY:")
    print("   - Plan for sustained engagement beyond initial launch")
    print("   - Consider how game age affects long-term performance")

# Run the complete analysis
run_complete_analysis()

Some key things to note about the data

Reviews

  • The category of reviews in the steam store are calculated based on a scale that takes into account the number of reviews that have occured and the rating of the review. For ecample if there is a game with 500+ reviews and there is a 95-100% positivy review rate it will be overwhelmingly positive. however if you have less overall reviews say 50-499 you only need to hit a threshold of 85% positive reviews to be in the overwhelmingly positive category. Steam requires higher percentages for better selling games as this prevents games with just a few positive reviews being labelled as overwhelmingly positive

  • the review_score number is a scale of 0-10 where 9 ~ 97% positive (Overwhelmingly positive). this score is normalized across all games. and accounts for review thresholds
